## Project Overview

This notebook prepares **CYBHI EBP/CDEP** BASIS-24 assessment data for analysis and reporting. It ingests the raw eInsight export, processes the two-row hierarchical headers, applies reverse scoring to items 4–9, computes total scores, and pairs each client's initial assessment with their last follow-up.

**Data source:** `Basis-24.csv` — eInsight Individual Assessments export.

**Scoring:**

-   24 items, each rated 0–4. Values that are non-numeric or outside 0–4 are set to `NA` (and counted).
-   Items **4 through 9 are reverse scored** using the formula `4 − raw_score`.
-   **The eInsight export already reverses items 4–9**, so the script reverses none of them (`basis24_reversed_in_export <- 4:9` in Setup). Evidence from the October 2026 run: the export's items are in the official order, and as exported, items 4–8 (as a group) and item 9 both correlate positively with the never-reversed problem items (r = 0.29 and 0.49).
-   Total score is a **weighted sum**: `sum(weight_i × rating_i) / (1 − sum of weights for missing items)`. Weights for Q1–Q24 are defined in the scoring chunk below and sum to 1.
-   Total score range: 0–4. Higher scores indicate greater functional impairment.
-   **A lower follow-up score indicates a positive outcome.**
-   `total_score` is set to `NA` if fewer than 23 of 24 items are answered (more than 1 item missing).

Subscale item mappings (documented for reference; **subscale scores are not currently computed**):

-   Depression/Functioning: 1, 2, 3, 9, 10, 12
-   Relationships: 4, 5, 6, 7, 8
-   Self-Harm: 11, 20
-   Emotional Lability: 13, 18, 19
-   Psychosis: 14, 15, 16, 17
-   Substance Abuse: 21, 22, 23, 24

**Pairing logic:** Clients are grouped by `client_system_id`. The first assessment is the initial; the last assessment (if ≥2 exist) is the follow-up. Clients with only one assessment are excluded. No minimum gap is enforced; `days_since_initial` is included so a gap rule can be applied downstream.

**Output:**

| File | Contents |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `basis24_paired_clean.csv` | One row per client: initial/follow-up scores, `positive_outcome`, `score_change`, quarter labels, `days_since_initial` |

# Setup

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(zoo)

# ---- Configuration: edit paths and reporting window here ----

start_date <- as.Date("2024-01-01")
end_date   <- Sys.Date()   # set to a fixed date (e.g., as.Date("2026-09-30")) to freeze the data window

# BASIS-24 items the eInsight export already reverses, so the script must not
# reverse them again. Checked October 2026: items 4-9. If the direction check
# flags an item after a new export, update this.
basis24_reversed_in_export <- 4:9
```

# Helper Functions

```{r helpers}
# ---- Shared helpers (identical across the cleaning scripts) ----

# Reads an eInsight assessment CSV export with two-row headers.
# Row 1 holds question text (merged cells export as blanks and are forward-
# filled); row 2 holds sub-headers ("Response", "Score", ...). Returns a data
# frame with combined snake_case names and fully blank columns removed.
# "0" is deliberately NOT treated as missing: it is a valid rating on most tools.
read_assessment_csv <- function(path, na_vals = c("-", "", "NA", "N/A")) {
  raw <- read_csv(path, na = na_vals, col_names = FALSE, show_col_types = FALSE,
                  col_types = cols(.default = "c"))

  h1    <- unlist(raw[1, ], use.names = FALSE)
  h2    <- unlist(raw[2, ], use.names = FALSE)
  h1_ff <- na.locf(h1, na.rm = FALSE) |> str_squish()

  new_names <- ifelse(
    is.na(h1_ff) | h1_ff == "",
    h2,
    paste(h1_ff, h2, sep = " - ")
  )
  new_names <- janitor::make_clean_names(new_names)

  df <- raw[-c(1, 2), ]
  names(df) <- new_names

  df |> select(where(~ !all(is.na(.))))
}

# Parses eInsight date strings in ISO (2024-03-15) or US (03/15/2024) format,
# with or without a time stamp. Warns with a count of non-blank values that
# could not be parsed (these become NA and are dropped by the date filter).
parse_einsight_date <- function(x, label = "date_completed") {
  x   <- na_if(str_squish(as.character(x)), "")
  out <- as.Date(parse_date_time(
    x,
    orders = c("Ymd", "mdY", "mdy", "Ymd HMS", "Ymd HM", "mdY HMS", "mdY HM"),
    quiet  = TRUE
  ))
  n_bad <- sum(!is.na(x) & is.na(out))
  if (n_bad > 0) {
    warning(label, ": ", n_bad, " non-blank value(s) could not be parsed as dates and were set to NA.",
            call. = FALSE)
  }
  out
}

# Removes demo/test rows (provider_id or client_system_id contains "DEMO") and
# rows with no client_system_id (they cannot be linked or paired). Rows with a
# missing provider_id are kept. Prints a count for each.
remove_demo_rows <- function(df, label) {
  missing_ids <- setdiff(c("provider_id", "client_system_id"), names(df))
  if (length(missing_ids) > 0) {
    stop(label, ": column(s) needed for the demo filter not found: ",
         paste(missing_ids, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }
  is_demo   <- coalesce(str_detect(df$provider_id, "DEMO"), FALSE) |
               coalesce(str_detect(df$client_system_id, "DEMO"), FALSE)
  no_client <- is.na(df$client_system_id) & !is_demo
  cat(label, "- rows read:", nrow(df),
      "| DEMO rows removed:", sum(is_demo),
      "| rows with no client_system_id removed:", sum(no_client),
      "| rows with missing provider_id (kept):", sum(is.na(df$provider_id) & !is_demo & !no_client), "\n")
  df[!is_demo & !no_client, ]
}

# Stops if the number of item columns differs from what scoring expects.
# Scoring is positional, so a missing or extra column would silently shift
# reverse-scored items and weights onto the wrong questions.
check_items <- function(cols, expected, label) {
  if (length(cols) != expected) {
    stop(label, ": expected ", expected, " item columns but found ", length(cols), ":\n  ",
         paste(cols, collapse = "\n  "), call. = FALSE)
  }
  message(label, ": found ", expected, " item columns as expected.")
  invisible(cols)
}

# Converts item columns to numeric. Values that are non-numeric or outside
# [min, max] are set to NA and counted (e.g., a stray "9" or text in a score column).
clean_item_scores <- function(df, cols, min, max, label) {
  num   <- df[cols] |> mutate(across(everything(), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x))))
  raw_m <- as.matrix(df[cols])
  num_m <- as.matrix(num)
  n_non_numeric  <- sum(!is.na(raw_m) & is.na(num_m))
  n_out_of_range <- sum(num_m < min | num_m > max, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (n_non_numeric + n_out_of_range > 0) {
    warning(label, ": ", n_non_numeric, " non-numeric and ", n_out_of_range,
            " out-of-range (", min, "-", max, ") item value(s) set to NA.", call. = FALSE)
  } else {
    message(label, ": all item values are numeric and within ", min, "-", max, ".")
  }
  df[cols] <- num |> mutate(across(everything(), ~ if_else(.x < min | .x > max, NA_real_, .x)))
  df
}

# After reverse scoring, every item should correlate positively with the sum of
# the anchor items (excluding itself). Pass the items the instrument never
# reverse-scores as `anchor`: comparing against all items can hide a block of
# reversed items that mostly agree with each other. A negative value means the
# item's direction is wrong (reversed twice, or a positively worded item that
# was not reversed). Returns only the items that need a look (empty = all fine).
item_rest_check <- function(df, cols, label, anchor = cols) {
  anchor_sum <- rowSums(df[anchor], na.rm = TRUE)
  out <- tibble(
    item        = cols,
    item_rest_r = map_dbl(cols, function(col) {
      rest <- anchor_sum - if (col %in% anchor) coalesce(df[[col]], 0) else 0
      suppressWarnings(cor(df[[col]], rest, use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
    })
  )
  n_neg <- sum(out$item_rest_r < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (n_neg > 0) {
    warning(label, ": ", n_neg, " item(s) correlate negatively with the rest of the scale; ",
            "check reverse scoring (see table).", call. = FALSE)
  } else {
    message(label, ": all item-rest correlations are positive.")
  }
  out |> filter(item_rest_r < 0 | is.na(item_rest_r))
}
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Read and Score

```{r basis24-read}
basis24_raw <- read_assessment_csv(file.path(in_dir, "Basis-24.csv")) |>
  remove_demo_rows("BASIS-24")

score_cols <- names(basis24_raw)[endsWith(names(basis24_raw), "_score")]
check_items(score_cols, 24, "BASIS-24")

# BASIS-24 reverse-scores items 4-9 (positions within score columns, which match
# the official item order); skip any the export already reverses
basis24_rev_items <- 4:9
rev_idx <- setdiff(basis24_rev_items, basis24_reversed_in_export)

# Official BASIS-24 item weights (Q1–Q24); sum to 1
basis24_weights <- c(
  0.069588, 0.106112, 0.070040, 0.025082, 0.027949, 0.029729,
  0.026978, 0.024052, 0.056511, 0.094193, 0.048262, 0.058638,
  0.038422, 0.016425, 0.022986, 0.024274, 0.030429, 0.064966,
  0.058904, 0.052358, 0.017836, 0.013450, 0.010047, 0.012771
)
stopifnot(length(basis24_weights) == 24, abs(sum(basis24_weights) - 1) < 1e-4)

# Weighted score formula: sum(w_i * x_i) / (1 - sum of weights for missing items)
weighted_basis24 <- function(vals, weights) {
  missing_wt <- sum(weights[is.na(vals)])
  sum(weights * vals, na.rm = TRUE) / (1 - missing_wt)
}

basis24_items <- basis24_raw |>
  clean_item_scores(score_cols, min = 0, max = 4, label = "BASIS-24") |>
  mutate(across(all_of(score_cols[rev_idx]), ~ 4 - .x))

basis24_scores <- basis24_items |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    missing_count = sum(is.na(c_across(all_of(score_cols)))),
    total_score   = if_else(
      missing_count <= 1,
      weighted_basis24(c_across(all_of(score_cols)), basis24_weights),
      NA_real_
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(date_completed = parse_einsight_date(date_completed)) |>
  select(client_system_id, collection, date_completed, total_score) |>
  filter(between(date_completed, start_date, end_date))

cat("BASIS-24 rows after scoring:", nrow(basis24_scores), "\n")
cat("Unique clients:             ", n_distinct(basis24_scores$client_system_id), "\n")
cat("Missing total_score:        ", sum(is.na(basis24_scores$total_score)), "\n")
```

Direction check on the reverse-scored items (an empty table means every item correlates positively with the rest of the scale):

```{r basis24-direction}
item_rest_check(basis24_items, score_cols, "BASIS-24", anchor = score_cols[-basis24_rev_items])
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 2. Pair Initial and Follow-up

```{r basis24-pair}
basis24_paired <- basis24_scores |>
  group_by(client_system_id) |>
  arrange(date_completed, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(
    n_assessments   = n(),
    initial_date    = first(date_completed),
    initial_score   = first(total_score),
    follow_up_date  = if_else(n_assessments >= 2, last(date_completed),  as.Date(NA)),
    follow_up_score = if_else(n_assessments >= 2, last(total_score),     NA_real_),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(follow_up_date)) |>
  mutate(
    # Lower follow-up = positive outcome (lower impairment is better)
    # 1 = improved, 0 = no change, -1 = worsened
    positive_outcome = case_when(
      follow_up_score <  initial_score ~ 1L,
      follow_up_score == initial_score ~ 0L,
      follow_up_score >  initial_score ~ -1L
    ),
    score_change       = follow_up_score - initial_score,
    initial_quarter    = paste0("Q", quarter(initial_date),    " ", year(initial_date)),
    follow_up_quarter  = paste0("Q", quarter(follow_up_date), " ", year(follow_up_date)),
    days_since_initial = as.integer(follow_up_date - initial_date)
  )

cat("BASIS-24 paired clients:", nrow(basis24_paired), "\n")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 3. Quick Check

```{r basis24-check}
basis24_paired |>
  summarise(
    n_paired           = n(),
    n_improved         = sum(positive_outcome ==  1, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_no_change        = sum(positive_outcome ==  0, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_worsened         = sum(positive_outcome == -1, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_improved       = round(100 * n_improved  / n_paired, 1),
    n_missing_outcome  = sum(is.na(positive_outcome)),
    n_fu_within_3_days = sum(days_since_initial <= 3, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 4. Write Clean CSV

```{r write-csv}
write_csv(basis24_paired, file.path(out_dir, "basis24_paired_clean.csv"))

cat("CSV written successfully.\n")
```
